description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: dentalpin/dentalpin. Labels: enhancement, help wanted, frontend, backend, compliance. ## Summary

Build a GDPR compliance module for DentalPin to help European dental clinics meet their data protection obligations. Health data is classified as **"special category data"** under GDPR Article 9, requiring enhanced protection measures.

**Non-compliance risk:** Fines up to **4% of annual revenue or €20 million** (whichever is higher).

## Core GDPR Requirements

### Data Subject Rights (Chapter 3)

| Right | Article | Implementation |
|-------|---------|----------------|
| **Access** | Art. 15 | Export all patient data |
| **Rectification** | Art. 16 | Edit personal data |
| **Erasure** | Art. 17 | Delete or anonymize data |
| **Portability** | Art. 20 | Export in machine-readable format |
| **Restriction** | Art. 18 | Pause processing |
| **Object** | Art. 21 | Opt-out of certain processing |

**Healthcare exception:** Right to erasure can be refused when retention is legally required (medical records). Must explain legal basis to patient.

### Consent Management

- Explicit, informed consent before processing
- Track: when given, what it covers, who gave it
- Easy withdrawal mechanism
- Separate consents for: treatment, marketing, research, sharing with third parties

### Data Retention

- GDPR: Keep data only as long as necessary
- Healthcare laws: Often require 5-15+ years retention (varies by country)
- Module must support configurable retention policies per data type
- Automatic flagging when retention period expires

### Breach Notification

- Notify supervisory authority within **72 hours**
- Notify affected individuals if high risk
- Document all breaches (even minor ones)

### Audit & Accountability

- Log all access to personal data
- Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs)
- Processing activity records
- Demonstrate compliance on request

title: # EPIC-008: Governance data warehouse: rollups, analytics, exports, and retention that agree
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: ZK-VOTE/ZK-VOTE. Labels: help wanted, Stellar Wave, Spike, ADVANCED. | Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | Epic integration |
| Area | indexer + rollups + analytics API + exports + retention + privacy suppression |
| Difficulty | ★★★★★ (extreme, cross-cutting epic) |
| Estimate | ~24 hours per workstream (multi-day program) |
| Status | Open epic — decomposes into spike issues above; do not start without reading linked spikes |

## 1. Background & Context

Governance data needs outgrow the transactional indexer: analytics queries (SPIKE-124 inventory with freshness SLOs), rollup precomputation (turnout/quorum/treasury trajectories), privacy suppression (small-set linkage per SPIKE-007/139 bounds), bulk exports (tax per SPIKE-145, auditors per SPIKE-144, researchers?), and retention enforcement (purge per SPIKE-129 schedule) — while the indexer was built for listings (SPIKE-077), not analytics: no rollup tables, no suppression layer, no export pipeline, no purge jobs (cf. SPIKE-127 queue), and event-schema evolution (SPIKE-053) breaks rollup logic silently. description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: ARPAHLS/skillware. Labels: enhancement, help wanted, core framework, security. ### Feature Description

To reinforce the **Permissive Fortress** governance model ([#413](https://github.com/ARPAHLS/skillware/issues/413)), this issue tracks adding standardized SPDX license identifiers and explicit copyright notices at the top of all core framework source files (`skillware/**/*.py`), CLI entry points, and skill authoring templates.

# Copyright (c) 2026 ARPA Hellenic Logical Systems
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
```

For community-contributed skills and template files:

# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
```

1. **Defense Against Attribution Stripping:** When developers or corporate teams vendor, clone, or copy individual Python files (such as `base_skill.py`, `loader.py`, or `secrets.py`) into their own internal codebases or agent harnesses, individual files frequently become detached from the root repository `LICENSE` file. title: Review alate's privacy policy for content that doesn't belong in a privacy policy
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: Tessellate-Studio/tessellate-pages. Labels: help wanted, P0. Owner request 2026-09-18: double-check `alate/privacy-policy.html` (v5 after #12) for anything that typically should **not** be in a privacy policy, and for anything legally required that is missing or weak. This is a review task: list findings with a recommendation each, and change nothing without an owner decision.

## Candidates already spotted (2026-09-18, while checking #12)
These are observations for the reviewer to confirm or dismiss. None of them is a legal opinion.

1. **§14: "Continued use after changes constitutes acceptance."** This is a terms-of-service clause. A privacy policy informs; it doesn't collect agreement, and under GDPR consent can't be inferred from continued use. The usual wording is "we will notify you of material changes" (in-app or by email) instead.
2. **§11 Grievance Officer shows a personal first name ("Saptami").** DPDP needs a reachable contact. Whether to publish a person's name or a role plus `privacy@` is an owner choice. Flagged because it puts a real person's name on a public page.
3. **Implementation detail: "AsyncStorage" (§7 Security).** It's internal tech jargon that means nothing to a reader. "Stored in the app's private storage on your device" says the same thing.
4. **Changelog-style history in the body:** "Crash reports previously carried an approximate country… as of September 2026 we strip that" (§1f). History usually lives in a change log, not in the current statement of practice.
5. **Age thresholds: 16+ age gate vs. under-18 parental consent for India (§11/§12).** The two sections are internally consistent, but the app only gates at 16. Confirm the India wording matches what the app actually does, so it doesn't promise a check the app doesn't run.

title: docs: EU AI Act high-risk date in COMPETITIVE-ANALYSIS.md was superseded before it arrived
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: arthurpanhku/dvalincode. Labels: documentation, good first issue. ## What

`docs/COMPETITIVE-ANALYSIS.md` cites **「EU AI Act 高风险义务 2026-08-02 生效」** as regulatory tailwind in three places — lines 88, 136 and 270.

That date no longer holds. **Regulation (EU) 2026/1744** (the Digital Omnibus on AI) was published in the Official Journal on **24 July 2026** and entered into force on **27 July 2026**. It defers:

- Annex III standalone high-risk systems: 2 August 2026 → **2 December 2027**
- Annex I high-risk in regulated products: → **2 August 2028**

The Commission's stated reason was that neither industry nor CEN/CENELEC would have harmonised standards ready, and the conformity-assessment infrastructure the Act assumes had not matured.

## Why it's worth fixing rather than leaving

The document argues Dvalin's hash-chain audit and Evidence Pack catch a regulatory wave. That argument survives — but a security reviewer who follows this file will notice the date passed with nothing happening, which undercuts the surrounding claims more than the correction costs.

**The tailwind is rescheduled, not cancelled**, and the doc can say so more precisely than it does now:

- **Article 50 transparency obligations have applied since the start of September 2026** — that is live today.
- Two new prohibitions land in December 2026.
- The quality-management standard to build against already exists.

So the honest framing is nearer-term in one respect and much later in another, rather than simply "delayed."

## Acceptance

- The three citations state the current dates and their legal source (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744).
- The distinction between deferred high-risk obligations and the Article 50 obligations already in force is explicit.

Sources: [Gibson Dunn](https://www.gibsondunn.com/eu-ai-act-omnibus-agreement-postponed-high-risk-deadlines-and-other-key-changes/) · [CSA — Deferred, Not Cancelled](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.or …

description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: darnitdevorg/darnit. Labels: help wanted, quality, module-baseline. ## Summary

After any successful `file_create` remediation, the orchestrator calls `update_config_after_file_create` with the hard-coded Python `CONTROL_REFERENCE_MAPPING`, which overwrites whatever the user had at that `.project/` path. The mapping disagrees with the TOML (`locator.project_path`) and with what the remediation actually creates:

title: Help wanted: legal path to Hearthstone shop / gold on Linux
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: DawnMagnet/hearthstone-linux-gui. Labels: help wanted, question. ## Summary

The Hearthstone shop does not work in this launcher on Linux: the store appears closed and the gold balance is not shown. Login and gameplay work fine (see #22, fixed in v0.2.3). This issue is a call for **community help in finding a legal way** to support the shop / gold display. Our primary goal remains **playing the game**, not the shop.

## Current state

- The native Linux Unity client has no `blz_commerce_sdk_plugin` library. Blizzard only ships it for Windows and macOS (plus Android arm64).
- This project, like upstream [0xf4b1/hearthstone-linux](https://github.com/0xf4b1/hearthstone-linux), ships only a **stub** in its place. The stub returns an empty product catalog and an empty balance, so the game treats the shop as closed and gold is not displayed.
- Checkout also depends on Blizzard's embedded `BlizzardBrowser`, which has no Linux build either.
- Upstream has already said that this is expected and has never been fixed: https://github.com/0xf4b1/hearthstone-linux/issues/81. Some people mentioned partial work, but no code was ever published.

## Why this is hard

**Technical:**
- **Wine bridge to the official Windows DLLs:** you would have to load Windows commerce/browser binaries inside a native Linux Unity process. This is very complex and fragile.
- **Reverse-engineering / reimplementing the commerce SDK or protocol:** this is a large effort, and it would also need a working checkout flow.
- **Loading the macOS or Android `.so`/dylib builds:** these target a different OS or ABI and are not realistically loadable here.

- The [Blizzard EULA](https://www.blizzard.com/legal/08b946df-660a-40e4-a072-1fbde65173b1/blizzard-end-user-license-agreement) prohibits reverse engineering, emulating or simulating Blizzard protocols, and using unauthorized third-party tools that interact with its services.

title: Add organization-wide policy, budget, and audit governance
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: Dusttoo/orka. Labels: help wanted, architecture, security, durability, area: scheduler, area: cli-ui, status: blocked, priority: p2, effort: large, needs tests. ## Parent and order

Post-2.0 Orka Platform governance. Blocked by the organization control-plane contract in #140, #132, #133, and distributed identity decisions from #142.

## Goal

Allow an organization to set additive safety ceilings, shared budgets, capacity limits, and audit retention without silently weakening repository-local policy.

## Scope

- Define organization, project, and repository policy precedence.
- Add shared budget reservation and settlement across repositories without double counting.
- Define global and project capacity pools while preserving repository-local admission.
- Record authority, decision, configuration, upgrade, and merge audit events.
- Define retention, redaction, and export requirements.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Higher-level policy may tighten but never silently weaken repository safety controls.
- [ ] Budget and capacity reservations are atomic and recoverable across supervisor failure.
- [ ] One repository's hard stop does not become an organization-wide stop unless policy explicitly says so.
- [ ] Every privileged decision records issuer, scope, reason, expiry, consumption, and resulting state.
- [ ] Audit export is deterministic, redacted, and independently verifiable.
- [ ] Policy changes are versioned, staged, and reversible before first affected mutation.
- [ ] Synthetic multi-repository tests cover contention, partial failure, and replay.
- [ ] No application or customer data is required by the governance layer.

## Non-goals

- Billing customers for Orka usage.
- Replacing repository branch protection or provider audit logs.
- Centralizing application production credentials.

title: RFC/EPIC: Introduce a Go enforcement sidecar and FastAPI governance control plane
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: aegisora-ai/aegisora. Labels: help wanted, agent integration. ## Summary

Split Aegisora into a local Go enforcement sidecar (data plane) and a FastAPI governance service (control plane).

The sidecar handles the latency-sensitive path for every governed tool, provider, or API action. FastAPI owns policy and identity state, publishes immutable policy bundles, receives audit events, and manages human review. The TypeScript SDK/runtime remains the developer integration layer and sends governed actions through the sidecar.

## Why

The repository currently enforces actions primarily inside the TypeScript runtime and includes a small in-memory FastAPI interceptor. This is useful as a reference, but it does not provide a durable control plane or an independently deployable, high-throughput enforcement boundary.

The split should preserve one logical authority while moving policy administration and database work out of the request hot path.

+-------------+---------------+

    +-- audit batches and review requests <-- Go sidecar
